subject: Re: MAP: performance gating and workload charter for Nebula pilot
messages:
From: Harrison Cole <harrison.cole@nebulahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: performance gating and workload charter for Nebula pilot

Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nebula's engineering and product teams are aligned on moving forward with a short PoC. Before we lock dates, our security and SRE teams asked for a clear MAP-style benchmarking charter that captures: workload slices, measurement harness, pass/fail criteria (latency / throughput / TTFT / concurrency), and what evidence Redwood will provide for our procurement sign-off.

Our hard constraint: the pilot needs an objective performance gate so we can make a go/no-go decision before the procurement window closes (target close: 2026-11-18). Can you draft the benchmarking plan and a proposed schedule we can add to the MAP?

Quick context on Nebula workload:
- Interactive clinician chat (short prompts, average 30 tokens output), peak concurrency ~80 concurrent users across regional endpoints.
- Batch summarization jobs (nightly, 10k documents), throughput-sensitive but latency-tolerant.
- Search-ranking embeddings for triage (mix of single-request and mini-batch).

What we'd like from Redwood in the charter:
1) Workload slices with representative request shapes and candidate performance SLOs.
2) Recommended evaluation harness (replay vs synthetic vs traffic-shadowing) and measurement windows.
3) Bench artifact list you will hand over (raw logs, p95/p50 TTFT, steady-state throughput numbers, KV/prefix cache metrics).
4) Proposed timeline and responsibilities (mutual action items).

Attached is our internal acceptance checklist outline — this will be the doc our procurement team references.

Appreciate a draft by EOD Thursday (2026-10-29) so we can iterate.

Harrison
Harrison Cole
Director of Platform Engineering, Nebula Health
[Attachment: nebula_acceptance_checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Harrison Cole <harrison.cole@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: performance gating and workload charter for Nebula pilot

Harrison — thanks for the clear context and the checklist. Draft attached and summarized below. I built the charter to map directly to the procurement checklist you shared so artifacts line up with sign-off gates.

Summary (high level)
- Goals: validate that Redwood can meet interactive latency SLOs at target concurrency, demonstrate steady-state throughput for batch flows, and produce reproducible TTFT and p95 latency artifacts for procurement.
- Measurement modes: 1) shadowed traffic replay for interactive flows (preferred); 2) synthetic load generation for stress/throughput runs; 3) nightly batch runs on reserved capacity for throughput stability.

Workload slices (representative shapes)
- Slice A (Interactive chat, low token count): 95% of production calls. Shape: prompt ~15 tokens, response ~30 tokens. Concurrency target: baseline 20, peak 80. Acceptance SLOs: p50 TTFT <= 350 ms, p95 TTFT <= 900 ms; p95 response latency <= 1.2s.
- Slice B (Embedding mini-batch): batch size 8–32, throughput target 500–2,000 requests/minute. Acceptance SLOs: aggregate tokens/s throughput >= 18k tokens/s on dedicated pool; per-request p95 latency <= 600ms when mini-batching enabled.
- Slice C (Nightly summarization batch): large context jobs, throughput-style metric: stable job completion time within 5% variance across three nightly runs.

Success criteria / pass gates
- Gate 1 (Latency gate): Interactive slice A must meet both TTFT and p95 latency SLOs in two of three peak window runs (defined below).
- Gate 2 (Throughput gate): Batch slice B must achieve target tokens/s on dedicated reserved pool with quantization profile specified in the charter.
- Gate 3 (Stability gate): No single run should show 200% spike relative to median on p95 latency; KV cache hit rate >= 85% for replayed traffic runs.

Measurement windows and run plan
- Warm-up: 30-minute warm-up per run to populate KV/prefix caches.
- Peak window: 20-minute sustained peak after warm-up for Slice A (repeat 3 times across different hours).
- Nightly batch: 3 sequential nightly runs on identical capacity to validate variance.

Artifacts Redwood will deliver
- Raw event-level logs with token timestamps (anonymized), per-request TTFT, request/response sizes, model variant used.
- Summaries: p50/p90/p95 TTFT and latency, aggregate tokens/s, concurrency histograms.
- A reproducible runbook and the load scripts used (k6 + custom harness) and a Jupyter notebook that reproduces the final charts.

Attachments and links
- [Attachment: slo_workstream_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)] — workload shapes, param matrix, and exact run commands.
- Drive: shared MAP folder (link below) with run artifacts and evaluation checklist.

Timeline (proposed MAP milestones)
- 2026-10-30: finalize charter (this thread) and sign mutual action items.
- 2026-11-02 — capacity reservation and dry run (internal Redwood-only validation).
- 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-09 — execution window for peak and batch runs (customer shadowing available).
- 2026-11-10 — delivery of artifact bundle and evaluation report.
- 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-15 — procurement review; target close 2026-11-18.

Notes / tradeoffs
- If Nebula requires strictly lower p95 for interactive flows we can propose a model variant with reduced context or scaled Dedicated pool; that will change cost. We'll call out cost/latency tradeoffs explicitly in the final MAP.

Next steps
- Confirm the workload shapes above and whether shadowing production traffic is acceptable for the interactive slice (privacy note: we will mask PHI in the logs and provide aggregated metrics if required).
- Approve the timeline or suggest alternate run windows.

I'll upload the spreadsheet to the shared folder now.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo_workstream_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
Shared MAP folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_MAP_docs

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: performance gating and workload charter for Nebula pilot

Jonas — quick operational confirmations from infra/capacity:

1) Dedicated pool sizing: we can provision a 4-GPU reserved pool for the execution window and attach an autoscale buffer set to +25% for burst testing. That should cover the Slice A peak (80 concurrent) with the default model quantization profile (q4_0).
2) Model variants: we'll run first-pass with redwood-rlhf-13b-q4 and, if requested, provide a second run with a trimmed 7B variant to show latency/cost tradeoffs.
3) Runbook: Karthik will own the harness and coordinate the dry run on 11/02; I will own the artifact ingestion into the shared folder and make sure logs are anonymized before handing to Nebula.

Cost guardrail: for the MAP we'll include an approximate per-run cost estimate in the spreadsheet (approximate $/hour for the reserved pool) so procurement has a sense of the run economics.

I'll be on the 11/02 dry run and will validate KV cache priming behavior.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@nebulahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Harrison Cole <harrison.cole@nebulahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: performance gating and workload charter for Nebula pilot

Thanks Jonas and team — this looks good and very thorough. We accept the proposed workload slices and the measurement windows. A couple of notes from procurement/SRE:
- Please include the model variant used in every artifact (explicit string) and the quantization profile.
- For the interactive slice, we want the raw p95 TTFT numbers as well as a histogram of TTFT by payload size (so we can see behavior for 10–50 token responses).

Procurement timeline: we will plan to review the artifact bundle on 2026-11-12 and aim for final sign-off (contract + PO) by 2026-11-18. If Redwood can deliver the artifact bundle on 2026-11-10 as proposed, we should be on track.

I'll upload Nebula's acceptance checklist (signed) after the internal review; for now consider this an approval to proceed with the dry run and the execution window.

Priya Sharma
Head of Platform Operations, Nebula Health
[Attachment: nebula_acceptance_checklist.pdf (pdf)]
